track: Computer vision for raster floor plans (CubiCasa5K symbol and room detection for exact counts)

key_findings.title: CubiCasa5K: A Dataset and an Improved Multi-Task Model for Floorplan Image Analysis (Kalervo et al., SCIA 2019)
key_findings.what: 5,000 mostly Finnish floor plans with polygon SVG annotations for 80+ categories. Split: 4,200 train / 400 val / 400 test (random). Image types: high_quality_architectural 3,732, high_quality 992, colorful 276. Baseline: ResNet-152 hourglass, 2 segmentation heads + 21 heatmaps. Test results: rooms mIoU 57.5, icons mIoU 55.7. Per-icon test IoU: window 66.8, door 53.6, toilet 62.8, sink 55.7, sauna bench 67.3, bathtub 26.7, closet 69.2. Polygonized output drops a lot, for example bathtub to 0.0. The loader (floortrans/loaders/house.py) has 52 raw icon names, including Toilet, Urinal, Sink variants, Bathtub/BathtubRound, Shower/ShowerCab/ShowerPlatform/ShowerScreen*, SaunaBench*, SaunaStove and WashingMachine. Its 'icons_selected' mapping drops Shower entirely. It has 65 raw room names, including Bath, Bedroom, Kitchen, Sauna, DraughtLobby and Outdoor. Room type is read from the SVG class 'Space <Type>'.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: Stoa's cubicasa5k files (colorful-11397.png, high_quality_architectural-12232.png) follow the CubiCasa5K folder layout <type>/<id>/. The SVG ground truth very likely produced the question answers. So we can build per-class labels that match the templates exactly: windows, doors, toilets, sinks, Shower+ShowerCab+Bathtub, SaunaBench/SaunaStove, Bedroom/Bath/Sauna/Kitchen rooms and one box per floor drawing. Do not use the default 11-class icon mapping. It merges Toilet with Urinal and drops showers. Leakage: train.txt/val.txt/test.txt inside the zip list folders. Map every Stoa image id to its split before training.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: Code: https://github.com/CubiCasa/CubiCasa5k (pretrained weights on Google Drive). Data: Zenodo record 2613548, one 5.5 GB zip, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Non-commercial only: fine for the hackathon, but a Stoa product would need permission.

key_findings.title: OldDeLorean/rtdetr-floorplan-detector (RT-DETR-L on CubiCasa5K, part of Architect-Ant arXiv:2606.10953)
key_findings.what: Unmodified Ultralytics RT-DETR-L (32.8M params), trained on the official CubiCasa5K split (4,200 train) for 60 epochs at 1024x1024. AdamW, cosine schedule, flips. Took about 2.3 h on 2xA100. Official 400-image test set, AP50 / AP50:95: door 89.8/57.5, window 89.3/62.2, wall 82.3/52.8, railing 55.0/27.4. Pixel IoU vs the CubiCasa5K baseline: door 66.4 vs 52.0. Inference about 0.1 s/image on GPU and about 2 s on CPU. The authors warn that heavily furnished plans give false positives.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: This is the best measured anchor for our time budget. It answers the key question: a 1024px transformer detector trains in about 2.3 h on 2xA100, or about 4-5 h on 1xA100, and reaches about 90 AP50 on doors and windows. Its weights can serve as a zero-training baseline for door and window counts tonight. They have no fixture classes.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: Yes. weights/rtdetr_l_autoresearch_60ep.pt (66 MB FP16), plus train/eval/predict scripts. No repo licence is stated, and Ultralytics is AGPL-3.0. There is no CubiCasa-to-YOLO converter in the repo.

key_findings.title: heypaprika/gdino: Grounding DINO zero-shot vs fine-tuned vs YOLOv8s/YOLOX-s on CubiCasa5K
key_findings.what: Zero-shot Grounding DINO-tiny on 400 CubiCasa5K test plans gets mAP50 = 0.0. Every symbol under 40 px is missed, and 53% of the boxes cover whole rooms or floors (321x too large for doors). After fine-tuning on 1,500 plans plus a class-token scoring fix it reaches 39.3 mAP50. The specialists were trained on only 1,500 train plans at 1024px. YOLOv8s (80 ep) gets mAP50 67.1, with AP50 (detection rate): door 86.7 (97%), window 84.6 (97%), sauna_bench 83.0 (95%), toilet 63.2 (94%), sink 60.8 (88%), bathtub 39.8 (67%), shower 18.4 (64%). YOLOX-s (Apache-2.0) gets 65.7 mAP50, with sink 74.8 and bathtub 44.7.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: Strong evidence that open-vocabulary detectors are useless zero-shot on CubiCasa symbols, and that a small supervised YOLO wins. It also gives per-class difficulty for exactly our templates. Showers and bathtubs are the weak classes, so plan extra work there: higher resolution, full 4,200-image train set, crop classifier or Claude check. The 97% per-object detection rate on doors and windows means exact counts on a plan with about 10 doors are far from certain.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: Code public on GitHub. Weights not confirmed. YOLOv8s is AGPL-3.0, YOLOX and Grounding DINO are Apache-2.0.

key_findings.title: AECV-Bench: Benchmarking Multimodal Models on Architectural and Engineering Drawings Understanding (arXiv:2601.04819)
key_findings.what: Counting benchmark on 120 floor plans, partly from CubiCasa5K, for doors, windows, bedrooms and toilets, plus 192 drawing QA pairs. Frontier VLMs reach about 0.74-0.91 exact match on bedrooms and toilets, which come from text tags. Doors and windows lag at about 0.09-0.39 exact match, often 0.40-0.55 on a looser measure, with 20-50% MAPE. OCR-style QA reaches up to 0.95.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: Direct evidence that frontier VLMs fail at symbol counting, so our current 'Claude places one point per object' method will be weak on doors and windows. The same models do well on text-labelled room counts. This supports a split design: a trained detector for symbols, OCR or a VLM for room labels such as MH/KH/PH/SAUNA.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: Code and data release not confirmed on the abstract page.

key_findings.title: MuraNet: Multi-task Floor Plan Recognition with Relation Attention (arXiv:2309.00348)
key_findings.what: Attention-based shared backbone with separate segmentation and detection heads, trained on CubiCasa5K at 1536x1536. Door/window detection mAP50 91.7 vs 89.6 for YOLOv3. It used a custom split and about 1,000 epochs, according to the RT-DETR repo.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: Shows that about 90 AP50 on doors and windows is the plateau, and that high input resolution (about 1536) matters for small symbols. Use it as a reference number only.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: No code released (per the RT-DETR repo comparison).

key_findings.title: Raster2Seq: Polygon Sequence Generation for Floorplan Reconstruction (SIGGRAPH 2026, arXiv:2602.09016)
key_findings.what: Autoregressive corner-sequence decoder for room polygons. RoomF1 88.7 on CubiCasa5K. Training took 19.4 h (stage 1) + 16.0 h (stage 2) on one RTX A6000. Inference about 0.52 s/image. The paper notes that CubiCasa5K annotations are noisy and that rooms overlap.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: A pretrained CubiCasa5K room-polygon model is downloadable. It can segment rooms for the bedroom, bathroom and kitchen counts and for verification overlays without our own training. Retraining is out of budget (35 h).
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: Code MIT. Weights on HF haopt/Raster2Seq (key 'cubicasa5k'), CC BY-NC 4.0, commercial use explicitly not allowed.

key_findings.title: Raster-to-Graph: Floorplan Recognition via Autoregressive Graph Prediction with an Attention Transformer (EG 2024)
key_findings.what: Predicts wall junctions and segments autoregressively as a structural graph, with room semantics. The authors release a dataset of more than 10,000 residential floor plans.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: An alternative path to room vectorization. Of lower priority than a detector for count questions.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: Code public on GitHub. Licence not checked.

key_findings.title: xmarva/floorplan-detection (MMDetection on CubiCasa5K, walls and rooms)
key_findings.what: Cascade R-CNN R101 / RetinaNet fine-tuned on CubiCasa5K for wall and room boxes, with box AP 0.474 / AP50 0.634 on the val set. Includes notebooks/cubicasa5k_to_coco.ipynb, which converts the SVGs to COCO boxes (4,200/400/400). It keeps boxes only and drops masks.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: A ready SVG-to-COCO converter we can adapt tonight instead of writing a parser from scratch. Extend it with fixture classes and floor boxes.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: Code MIT. Weights on Google Drive (cascade 712 MB). Data CC BY-NC.

key_findings.title: Public Hugging Face floor-plan detectors (v1nz/yolo11-floorplan-det, SamirShabani/Architect, mudasir13cs/floorcad-yolov8n-detect)
key_findings.what: v1nz: YOLO11s on CubiCasa5K for wall, door and window at 640px, test mAP50 0.411 (weak, the resolution is too low). Architect: YOLOv8m on FloorPlanCAD (28 classes including toilet, sink, bath, bathtub, doors and windows) at 640px, self-reported mAP50 0.877, CC BY-NC 4.0. floorcad-yolov8n: 35 FloorPlanCAD classes, AGPL-3.0. Dataset v1nz/cubicasa5k-yolo is a YOLO polygon conversion (wall/door/window only).
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: None of them covers our full CubiCasa template set at adequate resolution. The FloorPlanCAD models have a different drawing style (Chinese CAD). Useful only as weak baselines or to warm-start. Training our own is required.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: Weights public on HF. Licences CC BY-NC 4.0 (v1nz, Architect) and AGPL-3.0 (floorcad).

key_findings.title: RF-DETR (Roboflow, ICLR 2026, arXiv:2511.09554)
key_findings.what: DINOv2-backbone real-time DETR. Sizes N/S/M/L are Apache-2.0: COCO AP50:95 48.4/53.0/54.7/56.5, RF100-VL 57.7-62.2, T4 latency 2.3-6.8 ms. RF-DETR-Seg is also Apache-2.0. XL/2XL use the PML licence. A Roboflow-hosted RF-DETR-Base is trained on the 'cubicasa5k-2' Universe dataset (4,978 images, 3-4 classes).
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: A permissively licensed alternative to Ultralytics AGPL, with a strong fine-tuning prior on domain-shifted data (RF100-VL). RF-DETR-M or L is a good second model to ensemble with YOLO for count voting.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: Yes. pip install rfdetr. Apache-2.0 for N/S/M/L and all Seg sizes.

key_findings.title: D-FINE (real-time DETR with fine-grained distribution refinement)
key_findings.what: Sizes N/S/M/L/X, 4M-62M params, COCO AP 42.8-55.8 (59.3 with Objects365 pretraining), T4 latency 2.1-12.9 ms. Custom COCO-format fine-tuning configs are provided.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: Another Apache-2.0 detector option. Lower priority than YOLO or RF-DETR because its tooling is less turnkey for a 36 h build.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: Code Apache-2.0. Objects365 checkpoints may carry Objects365 terms.

key_findings.title: Ultralytics YOLO26 (also YOLO11/YOLOv12 in the same package)
key_findings.what: Sizes n-x, 2.4M-55.7M params, COCO mAP50:95 40.9-57.5 at 640px. NMS-free one-to-one head (nms=False), STAL small-target label assignment, optional P2 small-object head config (no pretrained weights), -seg and -obb variants. Licence AGPL-3.0 or Enterprise.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: The fastest path to a trained CubiCasa detector: YOLO txt labels, one CLI command, built-in imgsz 1280-1536 and mosaic augmentation. Small-target assignment fits 20-40 px sinks and toilets. AGPL is acceptable for a hackathon demo, but flag it for any Stoa product.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: Yes, pip ultralytics. AGPL-3.0.

key_findings.title: SAM 3: Segment Anything with Concepts (arXiv:2511.16719) and SAM-based floor-plan room segmentation (CIB 2025)
key_findings.what: SAM 3 does promptable concept segmentation from noun phrases or exemplars and is integrated in Ultralytics (SAM3SemanticPredictor). I found no published evaluation on floor plans or technical drawings. A CIB 2025 paper (Purdue repository) uses the original SAM with generated visual prompts, from as few as 5 reference plans, plus GPT-4 labelling to segment rooms and doors on CubiCasa5K.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: Given Grounding DINO's 0.0 mAP zero-shot on CubiCasa, expect weak text-prompted results on symbols. SAM or SAM 3 is more useful as a mask refiner: clicking a room centroid gives a room polygon for the verification overlay. Do not rely on it for counts.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: SAM 3 weights released by Meta (SAM licence, check the terms). CIB paper code not found.

key_findings.title: Florence-2-large (Microsoft) for OCR_WITH_REGION
key_findings.what: 0.77B params, MIT licence. Tasks include <OCR_WITH_REGION> (text with quad boxes), <OD> and phrase grounding. COCO OD AP 37.5-43.4.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: Finnish CubiCasa plans write room abbreviations in the image (MH bedroom, KH/PH/PESUH bathroom, WC, K/KK/KT kitchen, S/SAUNA, VH). A TUM report notes the CubiCasa model itself relies on these text labels. OCR plus a regex dictionary can answer the bedroom, bathroom, sauna, kitchen and separate-WC templates at almost $0, with text boxes as visual citations. PaddleOCR is an alternative.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: Yes, MIT licence.

key_findings.title: SymPoint / SymPoint-V2 on FloorPlanCAD (vector panoptic symbol spotting)
key_findings.what: Point-based panoptic symbol spotting on vector CAD primitives. SymPoint-V2 reaches 90.1 PQ on FloorPlanCAD with the layer prior, and 83.2 PQ without it.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: Vector-only (needs SVG/DXF primitives), so it does not apply to CubiCasa PNGs. It may matter for swiss_dwellings DXF or opening_design vector PDFs. Our DXF block/layer tools probably already cover those at $0.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: Code public on GitHub (arXiv:2407.01928). Licence not checked.

concrete_recipe:
GOAL: replace "Claude places points" for the cubicasa5k templates with a trained symbol detector and an OCR room-label reader. Claude becomes only the reviewer of uncertain boxes. Short answer to the key question: yes. One A100 can train a 1280-1536px YOLO or RT-DETR on the 4,200-image CubiCasa train split in about 3-5 h. The reference point is RT-DETR-L: 60 epochs at 1024px in 2.3 h on 2xA100, giving about 90 AP50 on doors and windows. Exact counts are harder than AP50, so tune for counts directly.

STEP 0 - data and leakage audit (Fri night, about 1.5 h, 1V100 $0.24/h or CPU). Download Zenodo 2613548 (cubicasa5k.zip, 5.5 GB, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) on a Verda VM. Read train.txt/val.txt/test.txt. Map every Stoa cubicasa5k filename (<type>-<id>.png) to its CubiCasa split, and print the distribution for the 320 preview drawings. Adapt xmarva's cubicasa5k_to_coco notebook and CubiCasa's house.py into a converter that writes YOLO and COCO labels for these classes: window, door, toilet (Toilet only, Urinal separate), sink (Sink/SideSink/RoundSink/CornerSink/DoubleSink*), bathtub (Bathtub/BathtubRound), shower (Shower/ShowerCab/ShowerPlatform; ShowerScreen as an optional class), sauna_bench, sauna_stove, plus floor (bbox of each floor group in the SVG) and room boxes or polygons by type (Bedroom, Bath, Sauna, Kitchen, other).

STEP 1 - template calibration (1 h, CPU). For preview drawings, compute SVG-derived counts per template and compare them with the Stoa answers. Example questions: do double doors count as 2, and does "showers+bathtubs" equal Shower+ShowerCab+Bathtub? This fixes the class-to-template mapping. It is calibration only. Never look up a CubiCasa SVG by filename at inference, which would be answer leakage and a disqualification risk. Write this down in the pitch.

STEP 2 - train (Sat 00:00-06:00, unattended). Use 1A100.22V ($2.37/h, --hours 7), or 2xA100 ($4.75/h) to halve the time. Main model: Ultralytics YOLO11m or YOLO26m, imgsz 1280 (try 1536 if VRAM allows), 100-150 epochs, batch 16, mosaic on, fliplr and flipud, 90-degree rotation augmentation, rect=False, using F1_scaled.png. Train only on the CubiCasa train split, minus any Stoa preview ids if we want a clean in-house test. Second model in parallel on the same VM, or a 4V100 ($0.98/h): RF-DETR-M or L (Apache-2.0) at 704-1024px. Estimated wall time 3-5 h each, about $10-25 total. Fallback for tonight: download the OldDeLorean RT-DETR-L weights for doors and windows only.

STEP 3 - count tuning (Sat morning, 2 h). On the CubiCasa val split plus the Stoa preview images that lie in the test or val split, choose the per-class confidence threshold that maximizes exact-count accuracy, not mAP. Add flip TTA and SAHI tiling (1024 tiles, 20% overlap) for images over 2,000 px. Use weighted box fusion of the YOLO and RF-DETR outputs. Flag a count as "uncertain" when it changes across thresholds 0.3-0.6 or when the two models disagree.

STEP 4 - room templates via text (Sat, 3 h, parallel worker). Run Florence-2-large <OCR_WITH_REGION> (MIT) or PaddleOCR on the plan. Normalize the tokens with a regex dictionary: MH -> bedroom; KH/PH/PESUH/SH -> bathroom; WC -> separate WC; K/KK/KT/KEITTIÖ -> kitchen; S/SAU/SAUNA -> sauna. Counting "MH" tokens with distinct positions gives the bedroom count. Cross-check with detector evidence (sauna_bench means a sauna exists, toilet inside a WC label region). Floors: count floor-group detections, or connected drawing clusters, plus "1. KRS/2. KRS" text.

STEP 5 - integrate into Drawing Desk (Sat afternoon). A new raster tool count_symbols(image, class) returns boxes with scores. The answer equals the number of accepted boxes, and every box is a citation in the existing zoom UI: numbered overlays, uncertain boxes drawn dashed. Only uncertain items go to Claude Haiku 5.5 as small crops ("is this a toilet? yes/no"), and Opus is not called for counts. The deterministic verifier checks that count == len(cited boxes).

STEP 6 - evaluate (Sat evening). Report exact-match per template on Stoa preview questions whose images lie in the CubiCasa test/val split and were not in training. Report the train-split images separately as "seen".

EXPECTED ACCURACY: these are estimates, not measured. Doors and windows: 97% per-object detection at 1500-plan training gives maybe 60-80% exact on plans with about 10 openings. Toilets, sinks and saunas (1-3 per plan): maybe 80-90% exact. Showers and bathtubs: weakest, about 40-70%, with Claude crop review needed. OCR room counts: maybe 85-95%. For comparison, frontier VLMs get 0.09-0.39 exact on doors and windows (AECV-Bench).

COST PER QUESTION: detector inference about 10-30 ms on a V100 ($0.24/h), well under $0.0001/question, or about 1-2 s on CPU. OCR is similar. Optional Haiku crop review on about 20-30% of questions adds roughly $0.001-0.003 each. One-off training is about $10-25 of Verda credit. That is also the "trained on Verda" story.
risks: Train/test leakage: Stoa's cubicasa5k images are CubiCasa5K images, and the full Stoa set probably contains most or all of the 5,000. A detector trained on CubiCasa train inflates accuracy on any hidden question about a train-split image. Report accuracy only on test/val-split images, and say so openly in the pitch.
Answer lookup by filename against the CubiCasa SVGs would give near 100% but is cheating. Use the SVGs for training labels and template calibration only.

Licences: CubiCasa5K is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 on Zenodo (non-commercial, share-alike), so derived weights are non-commercial. Ultralytics YOLO is AGPL-3.0. Raster2Seq weights are CC BY-NC. Fine for a hackathon, but a Stoa work-trial product needs RF-DETR, YOLOX or D-FINE (Apache) and a data licence.
AP50 is not exact-count accuracy: one miss or one false positive on a plan with 10+ doors makes the answer wrong. Thresholds must be tuned for exact counts, and uncertain cases sent for review.

Template semantics may not match the SVG classes: double doors as 1 or 2, door 'with leaf' vs opening, shower screens, urinals vs WC seats, balconies. Calibrate against the preview answers before training, or the model learns the wrong definition.
Shower and bathtub are rare and drawn in many styles (reported AP50 18-45). Expect the lowest accuracy there.
Small symbols (<40 px) in large images: 640px training fails (v1nz YOLO11s only 0.41 mAP50). Use imgsz 1280-1536 or tiling, which raises VRAM use and training time.

CubiCasa5K annotations are known to be noisy and incomplete (Raster2Seq and other papers note overlapping rooms and missing labels). Some Stoa answers may themselves be off, and an exact count can still be marked wrong.
Domain shift: a detector trained on Finnish CubiCasa style will not transfer to swiss_dwellings PNGs or historic scans without extra data. Route those to the DXF/PDF vector tools instead.
Open-vocabulary detectors (Grounding DINO, OWLv2, Florence-2 OD, SAM 3 text prompts) should not be the counting engine. Grounding DINO gets 0.0 mAP50 zero-shot on CubiCasa symbols.
Time: the 36 h budget allows one solid training run plus one retry. Start the VM tonight and set --hours with margin. Delete VMs after pulling the weights.

track: Fine-tuning small open VLMs (pointing / counting-by-pointing) for raster drawing QA - CubiCasa5K first

key_findings.title: Molmo and PixMo: open weights and data, counting by pointing
key_findings.what: Molmo answers count questions by emitting one numbered point per object (text tags, coords 0-100, ordered top-down/left-right), then the total. PixMo-Points has 2.3M question-points pairs on 223k images. Table 1: CountBenchQA / PixMo-Count test = Molmo-7B-D 88.5 / 84.8, MolmoE-1B 87.2 / 79.6, GPT-4o 87.9 / 59.6, Qwen2-VL-72B 80.4 / 55.7. An ablation shows that training with ordered points beats unordered points.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: This is the exact mechanism Drawing Desk already uses with Claude (count = len(points)). Here it comes from a small model that is trained for it. Each point is a visible, checkable piece of evidence for the 'visualize reasoning' criterion. Use the point format (ordered, numbered) for our own SFT targets.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: Weights on HF (e.g. allenai/Molmo-7B-D-0924, Apache-2.0, research/educational use per Ai2 guidelines). The card says vLLM <=0.7.2 because of a preprocessing bug.

key_findings.title: Molmo2: open VLMs with video, pointing and grounding (Molmo2-4B / 8B / O-7B)
key_findings.what: Qwen3 backbones (4B, 8B) or OLMo-3-7B, SigLIP2 encoder. Points use 0-1000 coords with object indices, and the last index is the count. Table 6, CountBench / PixMo-Count: Molmo2-4B 93.9 / 88.1, Molmo2-8B 93.7 / 88.5, Qwen3-VL-4B 85.5 / 58.0, Qwen3-VL-8B 90.4 / 65.0, GPT-5 90.8 / 67.2, Gemini 3 Pro 96.1 / 90.0. Point-Bench average: Molmo2-8B 68.7 vs Qwen3-VL 58.5. vLLM supported from v0.15.0. The repo has full pretrain and SFT scripts and checkpoints for every stage. LoRA is not mentioned, and the examples use 8 GPUs.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: This is the strongest zero-shot counting-by-pointing baseline at 4B. Run it on the preview CubiCasa questions in the first 2-3 hours, before any training. It is the fallback if our fine-tune does not beat it. Full SFT with the Molmo2 codebase is heavier than a LoRA on Qwen.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: Yes. Code at https://github.com/allenai/molmo2 (Apache-2.0). Weights at https://huggingface.co/allenai/Molmo2-8B (Apache-2.0, but the card warns that some training data is non-commercial research only).

key_findings.title: MolmoPoint: better pointing with grounding tokens
key_findings.what: Replaces text coordinates with tokens that cross-attend to image patches (patch, then subpatch, then location), plus a 'no-more-points' class. PointBench 70.7% (SOTA), ScreenSpot-Pro 61.1%. Other reports say counting drops slightly (CountBench -0.8, PixMo-Count -0.9) and sample efficiency is better.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: Shows that the field is moving pointing into the architecture. Do not build on it in 36 h. The point head is the part that 'next year's frontier models' will not make obsolete for symbol-dense drawings.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: The abs page does not confirm a weights release. The Molmo2 repo has MOLMO_POINT_README.md and a 'molmo_point' SFT config.

key_findings.title: Qwen3.5 Small (0.8B/2B/4B/9B), natively multimodal
key_findings.what: Apache-2.0, early-fusion vision, Gated DeltaNet hybrid. Qwen3.5-4B model card: CountBench 96.3, RefCOCO avg 88.1, OCRBench 85.0, CharXiv-RQ 70.8, RefSpatialBench 54.6. The 9B gets 97.2 / 89.7 / 89.2 / 73.0. Qwen3.5-2B CountBench 91.4/86.8 and 0.8B 77.0/68.6 (0.8B card). It needed vLLM main or nightly at release. Unsloth bf16 LoRA VRAM: 0.8B 3 GB, 2B 5 GB, 4B 10 GB, 9B 22 GB. LLaMA-Factory has qwen3_5 templates.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: This is the best quality-per-parameter open base for SFT: strong OCR (needed for Finnish room labels such as MH, KH, PH, SAUNA) plus point/box grounding. The 4B fits LoRA training on 1xA100 with lots of headroom, and serving it costs a fraction of a cent per question.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: Weights Apache-2.0 on HF and ModelScope. Supported by Unsloth, LLaMA-Factory and vLLM.

key_findings.title: Qwen3-VL Technical Report
key_findings.what: Grounding with both boxes and points, in relative 0-1000 coordinates (Qwen2.5-VL used absolute pixels). The counting data is a subset of the grounding data, with direct, box-based and point-based counting, and it includes PixMo points. The Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking chart shows CountBench 91.5 and 4B-Thinking 89.4. Molmo2's own eval gives Qwen3-VL-8B PixMo-Count only 65.0.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: Qwen3-VL-4B/8B is the safer fallback base if Qwen3.5 tooling breaks: Unsloth has Qwen3-VL SFT and GRPO notebooks. Its weak PixMo-Count result (dense counting) shows that zero-shot Qwen will under-count doors and windows, so in-domain SFT is needed. Users report coordinates above 1000, so clamp and validate.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: Weights Apache-2.0 (Qwen3-VL 2B-235B). Cookbook in QwenLM/Qwen3-VL. Coordinate pitfalls in https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/issues/1486

key_findings.title: Perception-R1: GRPO for perception (counting via detect-then-count)
key_findings.what: Qwen2-VL-2B, GRPO with a Hungarian-matched point-distance reward plus a format reward, trained on 10k PixMo-Count samples. PixMo-Count val/test 60.2/50.5 -> 78.1/75.6. Ablations: SFT only 58.0/59.9, with a thinking step 74.9/72.8 (thinking hurts), without reward matching 77.1/75.4. lr 1e-6, 8 rollouts, KL 0.04. GPU-hours not reported.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: This is the template for our RL reward: points matched to the SVG-derived ground truth, plus exact count. Two lessons: no chain-of-thought for counting, and RL helped where generic SFT did not. Counting training code is not released, so write the reward ourselves (about 40 lines).
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: https://github.com/linkangheng/PR1 (Apache-2.0). Weights Kangheng/PR1-Qwen2-VL-2B-Counting on HF. Only the grounding training code is released.

key_findings.title: Visual-RFT: Visual Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
key_findings.what: GRPO with rule-based IoU and classification rewards on Qwen2-VL-2B/7B, and on Qwen2.5-VL since May 2025. One-shot fine-grained classification +24.3% with about 100 samples. Few-shot detection +21.9 on COCO 2-shot and +15.4 on LVIS. 8-GPU ZeRO-3 example. About 200 steps are enough for a few hundred samples.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: Evidence that a few hundred to a few thousand verifiable examples move perception a lot. That fits a 36 h budget.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: https://github.com/Liuziyu77/Visual-RFT. Code Apache-2.0, data CC BY-NC 4.0.

key_findings.title: VLM-R1: stable, generalizable R1-style VLM
key_findings.what: GRPO on Qwen2.5-VL-3B for REC and OVD. In-domain REC improves steadily over 100-600 steps, while SFT barely moves. Out of domain, SFT degrades and RL generalizes. Supports LoRA GRPO and InternVL. The example uses 8 GPUs with ZeRO-3.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: A ready GRPO trainer with grounding rewards on the best-tested VLM (Qwen2.5-VL). It is an alternative to TRL if Qwen3.5 GRPO breaks.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: Apache-2.0. Qwen2.5-VL-3B checkpoints released. Paper https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.07615

key_findings.title: PointRL: point-level grounding from verifiable annotation evidence
key_findings.what: Turns existing boxes, masks and instance labels into pointing prompts. A hidden verifier checks parseability, point validity, instance coverage, count match and redundant or missing points. Base Qwen3.5-4B. PointArena overall 56.11% -> 65.58%.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: This is our recipe on our chosen base model. CubiCasa5K SVG polygons are exactly this kind of 'hidden verifier evidence'. The reward terms (coverage, count match, no duplicates) map directly to our counting reward.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: No code or weights linked on the abs page.

key_findings.title: AECV-Bench: multimodal models on architectural drawings
key_findings.what: Counts doors, windows, bedrooms and toilets on 120 floor plans, plus 192 drawing QA pairs. Models: Claude Opus 4.5, Gemini 3 Pro, GPT-5.2, Qwen3-VL-8B, GLM-4.6V and others. OCR-style QA reaches up to 0.95. Door and window counting is 'often 0.40-0.55' exact accuracy, and symbol counting 'remains unsolved'. The authors recommend tool-augmented, domain-specific approaches.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: External evidence that frontier models alone fail at exactly the 76%-of-questions task. This justifies a domain-trained pointer and is a strong pitch line. Per-model CSVs are in the repo.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: https://github.com/AECFoundry/AECV-Bench (data licence not stated)

key_findings.title: CubiCasa5K annotations (SVG) - the training signal
key_findings.what: 5,000 Finnish plans, more than 80 categories, 5.5 GB zip, train/val/test split files. The house.py parser shows the SVG groups: id='Door', id='Window' (polygons, endpoints taken from 4 corners), 'FixedFurniture <Icon>' (Toilet, Urinal, Sink variants, Bathtub, Shower/ShowerCab/ShowerPlatform, SaunaBench*, SaunaStove, ...) and 'Space <Room>' polygons (Bedroom, Bath, Sauna, Kitchen, ...). Licence CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: Every preview count question type (windows, doors, WC seats, sinks, shower+bathtub, saunas, kitchens, bedrooms, bathrooms) can be computed from the SVG. This gives exact point targets (icon centroids, door and window midpoints, room label centroids) and EN/FI QA with free ground truth. Stoa's own answers were probably generated the same way, so calibrate against them.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: Parser and code: https://github.com/CubiCasa/CubiCasa5k (floortrans/loaders/house.py). Data CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

key_findings.title: Swiss Dwellings dataset
key_findings.what: More than 42.5k apartments, 250k rooms, about 1.5M separators and 670k openings as WKT geometry in metres, with room types. CC BY 4.0.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: Swiss questions also ship DXF, so the existing native DXF tools should answer them at $0. Use the geometry only to make extra raster pointing data (doors, windows, toilets on rendered PNGs) if the PNG path is ever needed. Licence allows commercial use.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: Data CC BY 4.0. The Archilyse pipeline code is AGPL.

key_findings.title: TRL GRPOTrainer: VLM support
key_findings.what: Tested VLMs: Gemma3-4B, LLaVA-NeXT, Qwen2-VL-2B, Qwen2.5-VL-3B, SmolVLM2-2.2B. Qwen3-VL is listed only for agent training. Losses: dapo (default), dr_grpo, grpo, sapo. GSPO via importance_sampling_level='sequence'. vLLM colocate or server mode. QLoRA via quantization_config plus peft_config. The example is grpo_visual_math.py.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: The quickest path to a custom point reward with a plain Python reward function. Compatibility with Qwen3.5 is not guaranteed, so test it in hour 1 of the RL phase, or fall back to Qwen2.5-VL-3B.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: Apache-2.0

key_findings.title: Unsloth vision SFT and RL (GRPO/GSPO)
key_findings.what: Notebooks for Qwen3-VL-8B GRPO (4-bit, LoRA r16, max_seq_length 16384, fits a T4), Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Gemma-3-4B. vLLM fast_inference cannot apply LoRA to vision layers, so set finetune_vision_layers=False during RL. Example config: dr_grpo, 8 generations, lr 5e-6. Known Qwen2.5-VL 'addCriterion' gibberish, fixed with a reward penalty. The Qwen3.5 fine-tune guide covers vision SFT.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: The lowest-VRAM option. SFT and RL of a 4B model fit easily on 1xA100 80GB, so no multi-GPU ZeRO setup is needed.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: Apache-2.0. Qwen3.5 guide: https://unsloth.ai/docs/models/qwen3.5/fine-tune

key_findings.title: LLaMA-Factory supports Qwen3.5 and Qwen3-VL
key_findings.what: Templates qwen3_5 / qwen3_5_nothink (0.8B-397B) and qwen3_vl. LoRA, QLoRA, DoRA. A YAML config can unfreeze the vision tower for grounding (freeze_vision_tower: false).

key_findings.code_or_weights_available: Apache-2.0

key_findings.title: vLLM multimodal throughput on A100 (issue #24728) and Volta support
key_findings.what: 1xA100 40GB, ShareGPT4V images, unlimited rate: Qwen2.5-VL-7B 13.24 req/s, InternVL3.5-4B 15.61, InternVL3.5-2B 26.26, MiniCPM-V-4 17.59. At concurrency 1, about 1 req/s. RedHat's Qwen2.5-VL-7B card (older vLLM 0.7.2) reports about 0.7 QPS on 1680x2240 document images and about 2.6 QPS at 640x480, so resolution dominates. Several 2026 sources say current vLLM needs compute capability >= 7.5. V100 is 7.0 and has no bf16.

key_findings.title: FloorplanVLM: SFT then GRPO for floor plan vectorization
key_findings.what: Generates JSON wall, door and window geometry from floor plan rasters. SFT, then GRPO with geometric rewards. Floorplan-2M and HQ-300K data. 92.52% external-wall IoU on FPBench-2K. The base model is not named on the abs page.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: Domain confirmation that SFT plus GRPO with geometric verifiable rewards works on floor plans. Only the benchmark is promised as open.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: Only FPBench-2K is promised. No code or weights.

key_findings.title: Engineering-drawing fine-tune evidence, mixed: MechVQA and Blueprint2CAD
key_findings.what: MechVQA: 3.3K mechanical drawings and 21K QA pairs. MechVL beats the strongest closed model by 7.57 points after multi-stage training. Blueprint2CAD: zero-shot VLMs score 0.52-0.67 on drawing/render verification. LoRA adds only 'a few points' and makes the model's biases stronger.
key_findings.why_it_matters_for_stoa: Domain fine-tuning helps when the target is perceptual and well defined (counting symbols). It helps little for hard 3D reasoning. Keep the VLM narrow (point at symbol X) and leave the reasoning to Claude and the native tools.
key_findings.code_or_weights_available: MechVQA: the GitHub link is mentioned but not shown on the abs page. Blueprint2CAD (https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.02433): no release link.

key_findings.title: Other small-VLM options checked
key_findings.what: InternVL3.5 1B/2B/4B/8B (InternViT-300M + Qwen3; fast in vLLM, see above). Gemma 4 (2026-04; E2B, E4B, 12B, 26B-A4B, 31B; Apache-2.0; image budget 70-1120 tokens; pointing quality not reported). Florence-2 base 0.23B / large 0.77B (MIT; <OD>, <OCR_WITH_REGION> tasks; good as a cheap box detector or OCR, but no QA). PaliGemma 2 (3B/10B/28B at 224/448/896 px; a fine-tune base for detection). SmolVLM2 2.2B/500M/256M (Apache-2.0; DocVQA 80.0, ChartQA 68.8; no counting numbers).
